articles.summary: Hydro-Quebec, a Canadian renewable-energy powerhouse with major US export contracts, is stretching an investment plan worth C$200 billion ($143 billion) by six years to 2041. Until then, it anticipates potentially being a net importer of electricity.

articles.title: Majority of London’s Thames Bridges Are in Poor Condition
articles.summary: Over half of London’s bridges across the River Thames are in ‘poor’ or ‘very poor’ condition, the worst possible ratings, with the crossing in Chelsea deteriorating after heavy vehicles were recently diverted from a nearby crossing.

articles.title: Technology Stocks Lead S&P 500 Higher With Midterm Vote Underway
articles.summary: US stocks advanced as Americans headed to the polls on Election Day, with control of both chambers of Congress at stake and investors assessing potential risks to the artificial intelligence trade.

articles.title: Chile Pension Funds Breath Sigh of Relief as Swap Losses Narrow
articles.summary: Chilean pension funds saw returns rebound in October as a drop in US yields narrowed losses on massive interest-rate swap positions that have sparked anger from politicians and undermined faith in the system among savers.

articles.title: US, Venezuela in Talks on Fresh Aluminum Cargo in Trade Revival
articles.summary: Venezuela is in negotiations for a second shipment of aluminum to the US as part of a symbolic resumption of trade after years of economic and diplomatic disruptions.

articles.title: Midterm Election Trading on Kalshi and Polymarket Lags Prediction Market Boom
articles.summary: The US presidential election in 2024 served as a big-bang moment for prediction markets. Two years later, their forecasts on the 2026 midterms are getting plenty of attention, but the underlying trading illustrates how the platforms have struggled to expand beyond a few booming categories.

articles.title: Morgan Stanley Offers $2.3 Billion Debt for Dell Family Deal
articles.summary: Morgan Stanley has kicked off a $2.3 billion debt deal to help finance Baldwin Insurance Group Inc.’s acquisition by billionaire Michael Dell’s family office and Sequence Holdings.

articles.title: UK to Charge Builders 4% of ‘Your First Home’ Program Sales
articles.summary: The UK will charge housebuilders as much as 4% of the sale price on properties bought under the new Your First Home program.

articles.title: Treasuries Fall Amid Oil Price Swings, Strong Job Openings Data
articles.summary: Treasuries fell after a gauge of US job openings exceeded economist estimates, an indication of labor market strength with the potential to give the Federal Reserve leeway to raise interest rates to curb inflation.

articles.title: Sugar Slides to Five-Week Low as High Indian Output Jolts Market
articles.summary: Sugar slid after data showed Indian production is running well ahead of last season, deepening a slump that has futures down more than 13% from last month’s peak.

articles.title: Trading on US Stock Perpetuals Contracts Is Approved by CFTC
articles.summary: A type of so-called perpetual derivatives contracts tied to equities got the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission’s green light to start trading.

articles.title: Major Hedge Funds Mostly Lose in ‘Nowhere to Hide’ October
articles.summary: Many of the world’s biggest hedge funds extended their losses last month, as a sell off in technology stocks, a government bond meltdown and Brazil’s shock election combined to deliver widespread volatility and one of the broadest declines since the coronavirus pandemic.

articles.title: NJ Governor Warns Ports Against Russian Diesel Allowed by Trump
articles.summary: Governor Mikie Sherrill warned New Jersey port and terminal operators against accepting Russian diesel shipments authorized by the Trump administration, arguing that such imports would violate federal law and noting at least one tanker carrying the fuel may be headed for the state.

articles.title: A Luxury Cruise Exposes the Fuel Divide
articles.summary: Passengers aboard the Villa Vie Odyssey were told to disembark in Cambodia after the company said it couldn't afford fuel. Bloomberg Opinion columnist David Fickling explains how low occupancy and soaring fuel costs exposed the ship's financial weaknesses. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: NextEra Offers New Safeguards for $67 Billion Dominion Deal
articles.summary: NextEra Energy Inc. offered Virginia additional customer and financial protections, the utility’s latest bid to convince the state to approve its $67 billion acquisition of Dominion Energy Inc.

articles.title: Disney Targets 20% Cost Savings in Thousands of Layoffs
articles.summary: Disney is planning thousands of job cuts and asking some managers to target 20% in annual cost savings that could come from job eliminations as well as from expense reductions, according to people familiar with the matter. Geetha Ranganathan of Bloomberg Intelligence has more. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: AI Debt Fears Hit Fresh Record Highs on Supply, Profit Concerns
articles.summary: Costs to protect the debt of numerous US technology heavyweights against default hit fresh record highs Friday, with disappointing quarterly reports from Intel Corp. and Amazon.com Inc. spurring fresh concerns on whether the massive borrowing binge financing the AI boom will pay off.

articles.title: Meta, Alphabet, Intel Share Sales Leave Buyers Far Underwater
articles.summary: The plunge in shares for some of the biggest names in the artificial intelligence infrastructure boom has made a difficult situation worse for investors who bought into their mega-share sales.

articles.title: Containing the Binance Hack Hinges on Vow to Make Traders Whole
articles.summary: The $6.3 billion crypto heist that unfolded on Thursday evening was unprecedented.

articles.title: Investor Said to Look to Bid on Club Pilates-Owner Xponential
articles.summary: Fund 1 Investments LLC, the third-largest shareholder in Xponential Fitness Inc., the owner of Club Pilates and Pure Barre brands, is pushing for a take-private and is looking to buy the company itself, according to people familiar with the matter.

articles.title: Chile Copper Mines Deliver Worst Quarter in at Least Two Decades
articles.summary: Chile’s copper output slumped to its lowest quarterly level in at least two decades as accidents and wild weather compounded operational setbacks and the effects of deteriorating ore quality in the top-producing nation.

articles.title: Munis Head for Best October in More Than Four Decades After Rout
articles.summary: US state and local government debt is on track to notch its strongest October in more than four decades, as a relief rally follows one of the worst months for the bond market in years.

articles.title: Exxon, Chevron Deliver Big Profits on Strong Refining

articles.title: Big Oil Scores $56 Billion Windfall on Spiking Fuel Prices
articles.summary: Big Oil reaped more than $50 billion in windfall profits as conflicts in the Persian Gulf and Russia roiled energy markets and drove refining results to record highs.

articles.title: Wall Street Turns Ruthless as Earnings Misses Fuel Deep Selloffs
articles.summary: Equity investors are meting out some of the harshest punishments ever for companies that miss expectations, just as strategists sound the alarm that earnings growth has likely peaked.

articles.title: Lockheed’s Yearslong F-35 Deal Drives New Morgan Stanley Bull
articles.summary: Lockheed Martin Corp.’s multi-year fighter jet deal has won over one more Wall Street bull, who has also set a Street-high price target for the company.

articles.title: Everybody’s Business: Even Your Chicken Is Candy-Flavored Now
articles.summary: On this episode of the Everybody’s Business podcast, Bloomberg’s Joshua Brustein joins Max Chafkin and Stacey Vanek Smith to discuss DoorDash’s announcement to purchase Instacart for $17 billion, as well as the unusual mash-up of candy-flavored chicken. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Oil Is a Tough Trade for Now, Says Sarah Hunt
articles.summary: Sarah Hunt of Alpine Woods Capital Investment talks about selloff in tech stocks and earnings from oil giants Exxon and Chevron. She says even though some parts of the economy are doing well, some investors are still nervous about artificial intelligence. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Exxon Plans $100 Billion in Capex Through 2030, CEO Tells CNBC
articles.summary: ExxonMobil Holdings Corp. plans to invest more than $100 billion over the next few years to help augment global energy supplies, Chief Executive Officer Darren Woods told CNBC after the supermajor posted blockbuster quarterly results.

articles.title: London’s Stock Market Among Those Feeling Left Out of UK Budget
articles.summary: The UK budget failed to deliver measures needed to revitalize London’s three-century-old bourse, market participants said, despite its reassuring praise for the country’s capital markets.

articles.title: Milan Football Clubs Unveil €2.3 Billion Stadium Plan for 2031
articles.summary: The AC Milan SpA and FC Internazionale Milano SpA football clubs unveiled plans for a new arena to replace century-old San Siro Stadium, a redevelopment estimated to cost about €2.3 billion that will reshape one of Milan’s iconic sporting venues.

articles.summary: Deutsche Bank AG posted fixed-income trading revenue that outperformed Wall Street banks in the third quarter, showing how the lender’s effort to grow the business is paying off.

articles.title: Remy Cointreau Beats Estimates on Strong China Cognac Demand
articles.summary: Remy Cointreau SA’s second-quarter sales rose more than expected as demand for Cognac rebounded in Asia.

articles.title: Anthropic IPO Shutout Sends Asia’s Investors Into Proxy Bets
articles.summary: For much of Asia, getting a piece of Anthropic’s blockbuster initial public offering may prove nearly impossible. That’s pushing investors toward a collection of proxies, from the Claude maker’s listed shareholders to crypto derivatives and semiconductor stocks.

articles.title: Jio’s IPO Surge Ends Tata’s Reign as Most Valuable India Group
articles.summary: Jio Platforms Ltd.’s blockbuster stock market debut has propelled the digital company as well as its parent Reliance Industries Ltd. into rarified air. It also helped Mukesh Ambani’s conglomerate topple Tata Group as India’s largest conglomerate by market value.

articles.title: Healey to Scrap UK’s Standing Charges on Gas Bills
articles.summary: Standing charges on gas bills will be scrapped for millions of British households as soon as next year, Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey will announce today.

articles.title: RBNZ Governor Says Further Rate Increases Highly Likely
articles.summary: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Governor Anna Breman says further OCR increases are highly likely at coming meetings after policymakers voted 4-3 to leave rates unchanged. She points to anchored inflation expectations, subdued wage growth and weak domestic demand. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Princeton Digital Sees Strong Asia Data Center Demand
articles.summary: Rangu Salgame, Chairman and CEO of Princeton Digital Group, says India, Australia, Japan and South Korea are poised to drive significant data center demand as AI adoption accelerates. He also discusses the company’s financing strategy and focus on investment-grade hyperscalers. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.summary: UBS CEO Sergio Ermotti speaks to Bloomberg's Stephen Carroll after the lender posted third-quarter profit broadly in line with expectations, with a surge in client inflows potentially buoying the outlook for the global wealth manager. articles.title: Heineken Volumes Beat Estimates in Early Boost for New CEO
articles.summary: Heineken NV’s volumes grew more than expected in the third quarter as strong demand for beer in Asia and a rebound in the Americas gave Chief Executive Officer Rafael Oliveira a boost just weeks after joining the company.

articles.summary: BNP Paribas SA said clients in Europe put aside their reluctance and started engaging more actively last quarter, helping fueling a jump in revenue at the corporate and investment bank.

articles.title: Danone Sales Rise on Higher Prices, Medical Nutrition Demand
articles.summary: Danone SA sales climbed in the third quarter, driven by higher prices and persistent demand for its protein-rich yogurts and fortified drinks.

articles.title: China Refiners Tap African, Brazilian Oil as Freight Rates Fall
articles.summary: Chinese refiners are buying crude from West Africa and Brazil after a drop in long-haul freight rates cut costs, giving them more supply options as competition for Russian barrels intensifies.
